summary: Hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C:H) thin films were deposited using hydrogen plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) with CBr4 as the precursor and hydrogen plasma as the reactant. The films were grown at low temperatures between 150 and 350 °C. The study aimed to investigate the growth characteristics, conformality, and properties of the a-C:H films, including their structural and chemical composition, as well as their electrical properties. The results showed that the incorporation of bromine and oxygen in the a-C:H films decreased with increasing growth temperature, and the films exhibited good conformality on three-dimensional structures.
evidence: Hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C:H) thin films were prepared by hydrogen plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD). The a-C:H thin films were grown at low temperatures in the range of 150 –350 °C using CBr4 as the precursor and hydrogen plasma as the reactant.
